title: British Africa
capsule: British Africa designates the aggregate of British colonial territories on the African continent acquired primarily during and after the Scramble for Africa (formalized at the Berlin Conference, 1884–85), including the Cape Colony, Natal, Rhodesia, Nyasaland, the East Africa Protectorate, Nigeria, the Gold Coast, and Sudan under Anglo-Egyptian condominium. British territorial control peaked after World War I with the addition of former German East Africa (Tanganyika) and former German Southwest Africa mandates. Decolonization accelerated after 1945; Ghana's independence in 1957 was the watershed, with the bulk of British African territories achieving independence between 1960 and 1966, ending the contiguous colonial presence our dataset records through 1960.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Colonial administrative boundaries are among the best-documented in modern African history, established by treaty and surveyed over decades; however, 'British Africa' as a single polygon aggregates territories with distinct legal and administrative status (crown colonies, protectorates, mandates, condominiums), so the composite boundary is an editorial generalization rather than a single administrative unit.
